_what_this_is: THE PROGRAMME OF STUDY, IN FLIGHT. This file exists because the study's
PURPOSE kept being lost: the simulated runs were repeatedly described by
their success criterion (3 clean convergences) rather than by why they are
run at all. The founder had to point this out on 2026-10-03, and he was
substantially right -- arms 1 to 4 had each run twice, arm 5 had NEVER run,
and arm 5 is the only one that answers the effectiveness question.
A UserPromptSubmit hook reads this file EVERY TURN and injects a 1-line
reminder naming what is still outstanding. A compaction discards the
conversation; it does not discard this file. The reminder STOPS by itself
when every measurement carries a result and a headline -- `status` goes to
CLOSED -- so the mechanism expires rather than nagging forever.
rationale: To measure whether the fixes of the last 15+ days actually WORK. Clean convergence is the success CRITERION of the runs, NOT their purpose.
closes_when: every measurement below has result != null AND headline != null; then set status to CLOSED and the hook falls silent

supply_failure_taxonomy.why_a_taxonomy: The reach of the discrimination control is bounded by whether a corrected copy ARRIVES, and the live run shows that is not 1 problem but 3 distinct ones. A single 'supply is poor' figure hides which of them to fix, and they have different remedies.

modes.detail: the seat's quoted original passage does not occur in the target character for character, so it cannot be located
modes.remedy: a prompt-side instruction; the refusal already states it

modes.detail: the seat offering the copy does not own the falsifier under control; a copy correcting a different claim would mint a mechanical fault against a sound instrument
modes.remedy: none wanted -- this refusal is load-bearing and correct

modes.detail: the copy is labelled with a finding id that answers to nothing in the registry, e.g. 'DeepSeek-SIM_F006' where the canonical id is a C-number; 3 of these in round 1 alone
modes.remedy: mechanical: the registry summary already shows the canonical id, so this is a labelling mismatch rather than a judgement failure and is the cheapest of the 3 to close

supply_failure_taxonomy.the_route_that_works: DERIVATION from the seat's own proposed fix: 9 of 12 in round 0 and 3 of 5 in round 1. That route needs no donation from another seat and no verbatim quoting, which is why it is the one lifting reach.

spearman.why_the_tools_differ: scipy averages tied ranks and the numpy cross-check does not; they agree on sign and magnitude but not exactly, so this cross-check is weaker than an exact match

round2_discriminator_interim.verdict: MECHANISM NOT SUPPORTED. The correction touches a flat fraction of the target across rounds, so the cannot-fail jump at round 2 is better explained by CONTENT -- the surviving claims being vaguer -- than by corrected copies degenerating toward an already-fixed target.
round2_discriminator_interim.consequence: no fix is owed, which retrospectively validates the decision not to pause the run on that signal
round2_discriminator_interim.limit: the touched fraction is a proxy for similarity, not similarity; and an absent trend is weaker evidence than a trend would have been. To be re-run over all 8 rounds at run end.
round2_discriminator_interim.FIRST_DESIGN_WAS_UNWORKABLE: The discriminator first computed a difflib similarity between each entry's corrected_copy and the target text as the entry recorded it. NO SUCH FIELD EXISTS -- entries carry corrected_copy_target_sha, a hash. On real data it returned '0 entries in each group'. Writing it BEFORE run end is what caught that; at run end it would have read as an absent effect rather than an absent field.
